# Clipped unique-sector credits: an exact necessary area elimination

Let v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1), and let K be a planar convex body with 0 interior. Write X_i for the area captured by exactly cap i, and Y_i for the area captured by precisely the other two caps. All cap boundaries are area-null. Put k=|K| and q_i=|K intersect {v_i.x>=0}|. Suppose

    4/9 <= c < 1/2,
    q_i <= c k for all i,
    q_min+q_mid+q_max/4 <= k.

Let the six actual ray endpoints be (A,0),(-a,0),(0,B),(0,-b),(r,-r),(-t,t). Define the actual double-sector core triangles

    C_1=a t/2, C_2=b r/2, C_3=A B/2,
    C=C_1+C_2+C_3>0.

Let E_i be any proved upper bounds for the three unique-sector areas X_i. In particular the two-segment envelopes in `candidate 104bb1564dc1ac15` provide such bounds when their determinants are positive; use E_i=+infinity otherwise. Set

    G_i=E_i-C_i.

Then all G_i are positive and the following two necessary inequalities hold:

    max_i G_i/C >= 1/3,                                      (1)
    sum_i min(G_i/C,1/3) >= 4/(3c)-2.                       (2)

At c=128/279, the exact right side of (2) is 29/32.

## Proof

Put D=sum_i Y_i>=C and d_i=X_i-Y_i. Counting the six sectors gives

    k=sum_i d_i+2D,
    q_i=D+d_i.

The cap constraints and c<1/2 imply d_i<(sum_j d_j)/2. They also imply d_i=k-q_j-q_l>=(1-2c)k>0. Since X_i<=E_i and Y_i>=C_i, one has d_i<=G_i.

The sorted cap profile is equivalent to D<=3 max_i d_i: its left side is sum q_i-(3/4)max q_i, and sum q_i=k+D. Therefore C<=3 max d_i.

Hold the three d_i fixed and lower D to C. For each i the derivative of

    (D+d_i)/(2D+sum_j d_j)

with respect to D has numerator sum_j d_j-2d_i>0. Hence lowering D cannot increase any cap fraction. It also preserves the weakened profile C<=3 max d_i. We have proved feasibility of the following reduced, relaxed system:

    0<d_i<=G_i,
    m=max d_i>=C/3,
    C+m <= c(2C+sum_i d_i).                                (3)

No claim is made that the modified areas are realized by a convex body; in particular lower bounds for unique-sector core triangles have been omitted.

For fixed m, the largest allowed sum d_i is sum_i min(G_i,m). A component attains m exactly when m<=max G_i. Thus (3) is equivalent to existence of m in [C/3,max G_i] such that

    f(m):=sum_i min(G_i,m)-m/c >= (1-2c)C/c.                (4)

If min G_i<C/3, then for every m>=C/3 at most two of the terms min(G_i,m) are still increasing. Since 2-1/c<0, f is strictly decreasing there (piecewise linearly, including at its breakpoints). Therefore the best permissible m is C/3. Substituting m=C/3 in (4) gives exactly (2); the nonempty permissible interval also gives (1).

If min G_i>=C/3, then (1) holds and the left side of (2) is one. Because c>=4/9, its right side is at most one. Conversely m=C/3 satisfies (4) in this case, since (C+C/3)/(2C+C)=4/9<=c. This proves the exact equivalence of (1)-(2) with the relaxed system (3), and proves their necessity for the actual K. The restriction c>=4/9 in this equivalence is essential.

## Scope and a still-unproved algebraic step

The remaining proposed use would show that the actual six-ray constraints and ordinary inverse weight at most2/9 violate (1)-(2) at c=128/279. That implication has NOT been proved. A numerical screen `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/screen_clipped_sector_credit_root.py` is only a falsification tool; it does not supply a symmetry reduction, a global optimum, or a proof.

The smaller ratio-only conditions are false as a sufficient geometric obstruction. For example B=b=1/2, A=r=1/3, a=t=5/21 give ordinary first inverse weight exactly2/9 and all radial-convexity conditions, but

    G_i/C=(97/344,11/43,11/43)>23/96.

Here max G_i/C<1/3, so (1) correctly rejects the array. A separate rational array recorded by Slab also passes both the individual ratio tests and max G_i/C>=1/3; retaining the sum of clipped credits, rather than those weaker individual tests, is essential.
